header.userPrompt:
Make the bank-statement AI category/merchant suggestions reliable. Today they are computed by StatementSuggestionsService (server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/services/StatementSuggestionsService.scala), called from ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction. In production the stored suggestions come back with every row having no categoryId and no merchantId, so the review page shows nothing. Root causes, confirmed by reproducing the exact prompt against real data:

- The model is asked to ECHO category/merchant UUIDs and is sent a BATCH of up to 40 rows in one call. At that scale Nova Lite is erratic and non-deterministic even at temperature 0 (identical input gave 19/38 then 36/38 on repeat runs), and the prompt's "if no category clearly fits, use null" escape lets it blank out many or all rows.
- There is NO deterministic tier: the service feeds history only as few-shot examples to the model, never as a direct lookup, so repeated merchants depend on a model coin-flip instead of the category the user already chose.
- A silent short-circuit: `if (toResolve.isEmpty || categories.isEmpty)` returns all-empty suggestions with status Done, so a bug where categories fail to load is indistinguishable from "nothing to suggest".

BUILD THIS (keep the existing draft->confirm flow, the AiSuggestions model/columns, the background job wiring, the regenerate endpoint, and the review-page UI behavior unchanged except where stated):

1. DETERMINISTIC HISTORY TIER (primary, no model):
   - Add a user-scoped repository query that, for a normalized row description, returns the category the user has previously assigned to rows with that same normalized description — among already-categorized rows (bank_statement_row.expense_id set -> expense -> its single category split). Pick the most frequently used category for that description; tie-break deterministically (e.g. most recent). It MUST be user-scoped (WHERE user_id = ?) and have a stable ORDER BY. Normalize descriptions with the SAME normalization the rule matcher uses (reuse a shared normalize, do not invent a second one).
   - In StatementSuggestionsService, for each row to resolve: FIRST try this history lookup; if it yields a category, use it directly (no model call). Only rows with no rule and no history go to the model. This makes repeated merchants deterministic and stable across regenerations.

2. PER-ROW, NAME-IN / NAME-OUT MODEL CALLS (replace the batch + UUIDs):
   - Call the model ONE ROW AT A TIME (remove the BatchSize batching). Sequential is fine and preferred (the demo account throttles Bedrock under bursts); it is cheap, just slower.
   - Send the category NAMES (with the existing few-shot examples), not ids, and ask the model to return the single best category NAME. Map the returned name back to a category id server-side, matching case- AND accent-insensitively. Do NOT offer a null option for the category — force a best-guess pick (the suggestion is advisory and the user reviews it before importing).
   - Then, if a category resolved and that category has merchants, send that category's merchant NAMES and ask for the best merchant NAME or "none"; map back the same way. null/none IS allowed for merchant.
   - Mapping back must be unambiguous: if a returned name matches no candidate, or matches more than one (the data has a real near-duplicate category pair "Super"/"Súper", and merchants may share a name), treat it as no match (None) rather than guessing. The chosen merchant's category stays authoritative over the predicted category, as today.
   - Keep failing loud on unparseable model output (as today).

3. FIX THE SILENT SHORT-CIRCUIT:
   - `toResolve.isEmpty` is a legitimate no-op: store status Done with an empty rows list.
   - But if there ARE rows to resolve and the user's categories come back empty, do NOT silently store all-empty suggestions — log an error with the userId and FAIL the job (throw), so a categories-not-loading bug surfaces and retries instead of masquerading as "Done, no suggestions". Confirm categories are loaded for the statement's owner (statement.userId).

4. SHARE THE RULE-BASED ROW RESOLUTION:
   - The rule MATCHER (ImportRuleMatcher) already lives in lib/api/shared and is used by both sides — keep using it. The thing that is NOT shared is the higher-level "given rules + a row, what does a rule decide for it" logic: the web review page (BankStatementReviewPage.resolveImport) and the server (StatementSuggestionsService.selectRowsToResolve) each have their own. Extract a single shared helper into lib/api/shared (next to ImportRuleMatcher — NOT lib/common/shared, because it depends on the api models) that answers the rule verdict for a row, and have BOTH the web review page and the server service use it. Do not reimplement rule matching separately on either side. This is a refactor with no behavior change to the rule path.

CONSTRAINTS:
- User-scoped DB access (WHERE user_id = ?) on the new query; stable ORDER BY; no CHECK constraints.
- No silent defaults for missing data — fail loud (the short-circuit fix above is an instance).
- Log the new/changed work with the userId in scope (per the coding-patterns reviewer rule), after the user is resolved.
- Use Chimney for any case-class mapping; prefer enums over stringly-typed values; never drop a Future.
- Keep changes surgical; do not restyle unrelated UI or change the draft->confirm flow.
- Follow docs/guide conventions. Add/adjust tests for: the history-lookup repository query (user-scoped, picks the most-used category, normalization, ignores other users), the service (history-first: a row with history skips the model; a row without history calls the model once; name mapped back to id; an ambiguous/unknown name becomes None; category is forced with no null; merchant allows none; categories-empty-with-rows fails loud), and the shared rule-resolution helper.
